Yes. Desk is organized by requirement: each one has its own discussion, your decisions, how you can check it, and its tests, all in one dialog. The tree is organized by documents and test files, so the same requirement is spread over a design doc, a pending file and a board. That's Desk's strength, and why it should be the official view. It also suggests a split for A or B: the requirements, tests and state live in one tree file, and the discussions stay in Desk's log. I'd add Desk's log to the hourly backup, so the discussions have a copy too.

Yes, .gitignore:172-178: Desk's log (170 chunk files, about 2 MB), its seen-marks and your Desk voice file. That's why (A) matters. Two ways to give the official state a copy. (1) Un-ignore Desk's log and commit it: everything travels, discussions included, but every agent message and every line you've typed in Desk goes into the public repo. Your voice file stays ignored either way, because it goes to your vault. (2) Keep the log private and put only the requirements, tests and state in one tree file that Desk reads, with the log going into the encrypted backup. I recommend (2). Which one?

wsl-claude: yes, on purpose. Since 7811e88 (2026-09-27), .gitignore:169-178 keeps Desk's log, your typed lines and your 'seen' marks out of git: 'Andy's conversation with the agents... His words, never pushed.' Your typed lines go into your vault by hand.
That is why (A) splits it in two. The DISCUSSION stays private in Desk's log as now. Only the bare STATE goes into one file in git: each requirement's id, title, tests, pass or fail, and open, claimed or done. No conversation in it. Your Done would put the word 'done' in git, not your chat.
